subject: Tenant data retention, subprocessors, and legal-hold carveouts for VPC/on-prem
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@nimbushealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com, legal@nimbushealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 08:21:00 -0400
Subject: Private deployment — retention, access carveouts, and subprocessors

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are close to a procurement decision for a private deployment (VPC + on-prem backup) but have a few outstanding legal/security items that must be agreed before we proceed:

1) Keys & custody: Nimbus prefers customer-controlled keys (BYOK/HSM) for PHI. We will consider Redwood-managed keys only if we get contractual guarantees that Redwood cannot unilaterally decrypt or export keys (and we need an escrow process limited to court-order).

2) Operator access & breakglass: We need explicit limits — operator support may perform emergency actions but only under documented dual-authority and with immediate audit log delivery. Any exception should be legal/court-ordered.

3) Data retention & legal hold: Our retention policy for certain records is 7 years plus legal-hold exceptions. Can Redwood support a configuration that enforces customer-driven retention and legal-hold flags (i.e., Nimbus can lock records from automated deletion)?

4) Subprocessors: please provide the current subprocessor list and a process for notice/approval for additions. We also need confirmation no data will be routed outside the EU without our explicit consent.

I attached our DPA redlines and a short subprocessor matrix for reference.

Attachments: Nimbus_DPA_redline_20280409.pdf, subprocessor_matrix_20280408.csv

Can you confirm feasibility and next steps? Ideally we want a short addendum that can be countersigned this month.

Best,
Emma
Emma Stone
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
emma.stone@nimbushealth.com

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma.stone@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com, legal@nimbushealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment — retention, access carveouts, and subprocessors

Emma — thanks for the clear list. High level: we can meet the intent of your asks but need to lock down precise wording and an operational runbook. Quick answers up front:

- BYOK: supported. For VPC/on-prem we offer two recommended patterns: (A) customer-managed HSM (BYOK) where keys never leave your HSM and Redwood holds only wrapped key references; (B) Redwood EKM with a customer-owned KMS in your cloud account (we can provide the EKM integration playbook). Both patterns are compatible with PHI controls.

- Operator access & breakglass: we operate with JIT access, dual approval, and immutable audit trails. We can add a DPA addendum specifying breakglass conditions (e.g., court order, Pager escalation) and a notification SLA.

- Retention/legal hold: we can expose retention policies as a customer-configurable control. For on-prem, retention and legal-hold flags will be enforced in your storage layer — Redwood will honor those flags and provide exportable manifests for any holds. For hosted-managed components we will include contractual guarantees around retention enforcement and deletion attestation.

- Subprocessors & geo fence: attaching the most recent subprocessor matrix; we will commit to 30 days notice for changes and an opt-out path for material additions. For EU-residency we can geo-fence processing to EU regions and document that in the addendum.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood security and legal will produce a short addendum that maps to your redlines (we'll mark changes and indicate operational controls) — target draft by EOD Thu (2028-04-12).
2) Rishi will scope the onboarding steps and provide a provisioning checklist for BYOK/EKM.
3) Monica will coordinate SOC2/Security artifacts and a live review session with your security team.

Attaching: operator_breakglass_playbook_20280410.pdf (draft) and the subprocessor matrix we maintain.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync Thurs morning to walk through the addendum?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: operator_breakglass_playbook_20280410.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Stone <emma.stone@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com, legal@nimbushealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment — retention, access carveouts, and subprocessors

Emma/Laura — technical clarifications and proposed operational controls below. I wanted to make these explicit so legal can map to contract language:

- BYOK/HSM pattern: we recommend RH-1: Customer HSM hosted in customer VPC (recommended for PHI). In this model, Redwood never has raw key material. We store only key IDs and wrapped blobs that cannot be unwrapped without the HSM. Provisioning requires an initial key wrap operation during onboarding; we will provide automation scripts for common vendors (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, Thales).

- EKM pattern: RH-2 EKM where you control rotation and keys via your KMS but Redwood can call a customer-side EKM endpoint. This provides operational ease while keeping crypto control in your account.

- Breakglass: implement a JIT access flow with 2-person approval (one from Redwood SRE on call, one from Nimbus security or legal). All breakglass sessions emit full session telemetry (command hashes, start/end, operator id) and logs are pushed to your logging endpoint in near-real-time. We will include an encrypted evidence bundle delivery (signed) after any breakglass.

- Retention/legal-hold enforcement: For VPC/on-prem we will surface a retention API that respects hold flags and returns attestations of deletion attempts. The recommended pattern is to enforce legal-hold in your storage layer (object lock/immutable retention) and have Redwood reference the state. For hosted components we will include a contractual attestation and third-party audit visibility under the DPA addendum.

- Subprocessors: current list (summary): telemetry aggregator (EU-hosted), CDN for static artifacts (EU edge), support ticketing provider (US-hosted — we can carve PII out). Full CSV attached. Process: 30-day notice + right to review; for material changes we offer a mitigation path (sprint-delivery to remove certain data flows).

Open items for legal: define exact thresholds for "material" subprocessor additions, carveouts for support data minimization, and precise wording for escrow access (court-order only; we can require a formal legal request + sealed court order + dual internal approvals).

Happy to walk through the playbook in the Thursday sync.

-Rishi

From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@nimbushealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com, legal@nimbushealth.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment — retention, access carveouts, and subprocessors

Laura/Rishi — appreciate the quick turnaround.

We reviewed your playbook and the proposed patterns. Nimbus confirms we prefer RH-1 (customer HSM in our VPC). Please proceed with the addendum that:

- Names RH-1 as the default key custody pattern for our tenancy.
- Requires Redwood to provide signed attestations after any breakglass session and to push audit bundles to our secure S3 endpoint within 6 hours.
- Commits to EU-only processing for our tenancy and a 30-day notice for subprocessors; for any new material subprocessor we reserve the right to pause onboarding until mitigation is agreed.
- Specifies legal-hold enforcement as a customer-controlled flag that Redwood will not override.

Procurement asks for a final addendum and DocuSign wrapper. Can you route the DPA + addendum to https://docusign.net/envelopes/E-1234567890 and cc procurement? If you can get the countersigned doc back by 2028-04-20 we can start provisioning the BYOK flow the following week.

Thanks — will plan to join the Thursday sync for the technical run-through.

Emma
